title: fix(types): mirror `wrapperClass` on `InputSchema`, the last unexamined `schema.wrapperClass` reader (objectui#8072)
body:
Fixes #8072

`renderers/form/input.tsx` reads `cn("grid w-full items-center gap-1.5", schema.wrapperClass)`. The TypeScript face has declared the key all along (`form.ts`, docblock "Input wrapper CSS class"); the zod mirror never did, so the value rode through `.passthrough()` and `{ type: 'input', wrapperClass: 42 }` validated **green** — while the identical document on any of the other eight `schema.wrapperClass` readers was refused at the key.

## The premise, re-derived BY BLOCK rather than by keyword

A bare `grep wrapperClass` over `form.zod.ts` hits three sites that read like "it is already there". They belong to the neighbours. Parsing the file into its `export const` blocks and asking per block:

| block | lines | `wrapperClass` declared |
|---|---|---|
| **`InputSchema`** | 214-241 | **no** — the subject |
| `TextareaSchema` | 242-278 | yes |
| `SelectSchema` | 279-313 | yes |
| `CheckboxSchema` | 314-347 | yes — the form copied here |

The renderer read is live and unchanged; `input.tsx` and the TS face are untouched by this branch.

## The four census figures, derived off the file and shown

The card's step 2 quoted `14 entries / 87 keys — 2 / 3 spec-derived, 12 / 84 local`. **All four were stale** — objectui#7762 had moved every one of them, and the file's own sentences say so. Re-derived with the same instrument the census uses (`ledgerEntryMembers`, the file's TypeScript AST, union arms walked) plus `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` membership, before and after:

| figure | on this branch's base | after this change |
|---|---|---|
| `UnmirroredDeclared` total | 14 entries / 86 keys | **13 / 85** |
| SPEC-DERIVED half | 3 entries / 17 keys | **3 / 17 — unmoved** |
| LOCAL half | 11 entries / 69 keys | **10 / 68** |
| entry-count restatement and the union of the two unmirrored ledgers | 14 pairs, 14 pairs | **13, 13** |

The working, in one line each:

- `UnmirroredDeclared['form.zod.ts#InputSchema']` carried **exactly one arm**, `wrapperClass`. Removing the key therefore emptied the entry, so entry count and key total move **together** — unlike objectui#7762, which took one key off a fifteen-key entry and moved only the key total. That is the trap in the obvious arithmetic, and it lands on the safe side here.
- The pair's **other** map membership is `KnownDrift`, not this ledger: `'form.zod.ts#InputSchema': 'onChange'`, a runtime slot the mirror refuses by name. `KnownDrift` is untouched, and its own figures did not move.
- `form.zod.ts#InputSchema` is **not** in `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS`, so the whole move lands in the LOCAL half and the SPEC-DERIVED figures stay put.
- `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` holds three entries, none of them this pair, and it is a subset of `UnmirroredDeclared` — so the union shrinks with the ledger and the subset leg stays true.

**Seven prose sites move, not four.** The card and the dispatch between them name the top-of-file bullet, the two split bullets and the totals line; the census also reads the cross-ledger sentence (two figures) and **both** ledger docstrings' key totals, which live in different paragraphs. All seven are corrected, each with the cumulative history sentence its section keeps. Every one is pinned: the four census blocks are green.

## The pin: accepted to refused, with three controls

New file `packages/types/src/__tests__/input-wrapper-class-mirrored-8072.test.ts`. Run against this branch's base **before** the mirror moved, it failed on exactly the legs that should fail and passed the controls — 11 passed, 4 failed:

- `{ type: 'input', wrapperClass: 42 }` **accepted** on the mirror and through `safeValidateSchema`; `wrapperClass` absent from a 33-key shape.
- the strict authoring face **refused** an authored *string* `wrapperClass` on `input`.
- **control, passing before the change**: the same wrong-typed document on the `checkbox` sibling was already refused at the key — this branch touches no mirror but `InputSchema`, so that leg reads the same on either side of it.
- **control**: an authored string `wrapperClass` on `input` parses green on both faces and the value survives the parse.
- **control**: an undeclared key of any type is still admitted unexamined, so the unknown-key policy did not move.

After the change all legs pass.

## One direction the dispatch did not name: the derived STRICT face moves the OPPOSITE way

`StrictAnyComponentSchema` (objectui#8345) is derived from these mirrors and closes unknown keys, so before this change it **refused** an authored string `wrapperClass` on `input` — the exact spelling the published TypeScript declaration invites an author to write. It parses now. Measured, not reasoned: that leg failed on the base tree and passes here. The two faces move apart — the tolerant one narrows, the strict one stops contradicting the TS declaration — and both are pinned.

This does **not** move clause 2: the key is already on the published TypeScript face, so the strict face is being pulled back to a declaration that already shipped, and the published TS surface does not move by one byte.

## Reverse verification

Committed first, then the declaration was deleted from `form.zod.ts` and the pins re-run. The mutation was proved on disk before the run — anchor text 1 occurrence to 0, blob hash `2a664196b` to `022429bdf` — and the restore proved by hash equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, not by an exit code. The test reaches the mirror through a relative source import, so no build sits in the path.

Six legs turned red, and which six is the useful part:

- the three accept-to-refuse legs;
- objectui#7722's sweep leg `declares wrapperClass on the zod face ... unless ledgered` — proof the exemption was really deleted rather than left covering the case;
- `InputShorthandSchema declares it and refuses the wrong-typed value` — proof the removed local re-declaration is genuinely supplied by `InputSchema` through the `.omit()`;
- the strict-face leg.

The three controls stayed green under the mutant. 77 passed alongside the 6 failures; restored, all green again.

⚠️ First attempt at this ablation was **read as a no-op and re-run**: the marker I grepped (`objectui#8072` plus a closing paren) also matched a second, untouched comment, so the post-mutation count read 1 instead of 0 and the script refused the reading and restored. The anchor was re-pointed at text unique to the removed declaration. The mutation had in fact landed; the guard was measuring the wrong thing, which is the failure it exists to catch.

## Step 3 was deleted, not weakened

`LEDGERED_UNMIRRORED` in `wrapper-class-declared-7722.test.ts` is empty now, and its docblock records that the exemption expired as designed. The sweep judges all nine readers alike. The exemption's two conditions — mirror still lacks the key, ledger row still on disk — are both false, which is what turned it red the moment step 1 landed.

## Also in this branch

- `InputShorthandSchema` stops re-declaring `wrapperClass` locally. That declaration existed only because `InputSchema` lacked it, and its comment said so in as many words; with the row shrunk, the arm inherits the key through the `.omit()` like every other key. Its membership and refusal are pinned, and the ablation above shows the pin can fail. The comment it replaces also carried a cross-file line address, which the house rule bans.
- `.changeset/7722-wrapper-class-five-more.md` — prose only, frontmatter untouched. Its closing sentence said this row "stays there" and the exemption is carried; both go false at release time with this change pending beside it. `check:changeset-claims` reports that read, names correcting the body as the remedy, and `check:changeset-overwrite` records the write as its own case 2.

## Verification

Commit `67ac055d6`.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` — green (all three tsconfigs: `--noEmit`, examples, test).
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` — **205 files, 4786 tests, all passing**. Run through the shared serialisation lock; `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types lint` — **0 errors** (290 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings, none in a file this branch touches). 276 files linted, read from the `--format json` output; all four touched files score 0 errors and 0 warnings. The narrowing to one package is sound because this repo's ESLint is **not** type-aware — `tseslint.configs.recommended`, no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, zero type-checked rules — so no file this branch does not touch can change verdict.
- Gates run green: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new, and one existing cross-file address removed), `check:test-path-roots`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check-changeset-presence`.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed:

- `.changeset/pin-ledger-docstring-key-totals.md` states in the present tense that two instruments "measure **87**". That figure was already stale on this branch's base — objectui#7762 took the ledger to 86 — so it is **not** falsified by this change and is left alone. Whoever next touches that changeset is the carrier.
- The docs half of this key set is objectui#8095's: the page set for `wrapperClass` grows from five to six now that `input` mirrors it. Not touched here, as the triage note asked.
- `LEDGERED_UNMIRRORED` is now an empty map, so the exemption test iterates nothing and passes vacuously. It is a ratchet sitting at zero rather than a defect; the docblock says so and says a new row expires the same way.
- The other keys of `UnmirroredDeclared` are that ledger's worklist and were not swept.
